description: The chart illustrates the difference in average word error rate (WER) from a “Whisper large” baseline for two fine-tuned models across several text “Optimisations applied.” The category axis is vertical and labeled “Optimisations applied,” listing five categories from top to bottom: Normalised, Add Spacing, Remove Spacing, Americanisms, and Dates. The value axis is horizontal and labeled “Difference in Average WER from Whisper large,” shown on a linear scale with tick marks at approximately 0.000, 0.001, 0.002, and 0.003 (values extend slightly beyond 0.003). Each category contains two horizontally aligned bars (a grouped layout): a brown bar for the “NESAC ft model” and a dark green bar for the “SESHA ft model,” as indicated by the legend titled “Model” below the plot. For Normalised, the NESAC bar is labeled about 0.00334 and the SESHA bar about 0.00323; for Add Spacing, NESAC is about 0.00319 and SESHA about 0.00344; for Remove Spacing, NESAC is about 0.00311 and SESHA about 0.00306; for Americanisms, NESAC is about 0.00299 and SESHA about 0.00302; and for Dates, NESAC is about 0.00257 and SESHA about 0.00228. The bars are not visually sorted by magnitude (they follow the listed optimization order), and there are no special highlights beyond the numeric value annotations placed near the right ends of the bars.
